scenes.say: Ever wonder why some firewall rules feel simple, while others get messy fast? Let’s break down what makes a firewall stateful, and why you’ll care in interviews.
Stateful firewalls keep track of connections, so replies get through automatically. With stateless rules, you need to allow traffic both ways, or things break.
When you file a firewall request, always include the source and destination, the port and protocol, direction, and why you need it. Miss one, and your ticket gets bounced.

scenes.title: Testing a new rule
scenes.say: After your rule is in, test it. Use netcat on Linux or Test Net Connection on Windows to make sure traffic actually flows.

scenes.question: Backend calls client—need a rule?
scenes.right: Yes. If the backend initiates, you need a rule for that direction too.
scenes.say: Here’s a classic trap: if your backend calls back to the client, you need a rule for that direction—even with stateful firewalls. Don’t miss it in interviews.
